feedback: If a learner describes one continuous electrical wire with no gap, highlight the synaptic gap: at the chemical synapses modelled here, neurons do not touch; a neurotransmitter bridges the gap and can begin a fresh impulse in the next cell.
If a learner treats the whole signal as purely electrical, name the two steps explicitly — electrical along the axon, chemical across the synapse — so 'electro-chemical' is grounded.
When myelin is added and the impulse speeds up, link it to insulation speeding transmission (kept qualitative, not biochemical).
activities.intendedInsight: The brain's signal is not one continuous wire but a chain of cells passing an electro-chemical baton: electrical along the axon, chemical across the synapse. Myelin acts as insulation that speeds the impulse.
learnerActions: Fire an impulse and trace it along the axon of one neuron to the synapse.
At the synaptic gap, describe/show how a chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) crosses the gap and can start a NEW impulse in the next neuron.
Add a myelin sheath and compare the impulse speed with and without it.
State in your own words why the signal is 'electro-chemical' rather than one continuous electrical wire.
activities.title: Build and run a neuron relay (signalling + myelin)
